title: Number of simple graphs on a finite vertex set
statement: For every natural number $n$, the number of simple graphs on the vertex set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ equals $2^{\binom{n}{2}}$, since a simple graph is determined by choosing which of the $\binom{n}{2}$ possible unordered pairs of distinct vertices form edges.
hypotheses_covered: n : ℕ (an arbitrary natural number, indexing the vertex set)
replaced:
Denote by $\mathcal{G}_n$ the set of simple graphs with vertex set
$\{v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n\}$ [...] Clearly
\[|\mathcal{G}_n| = 2^{\binom{n}{2}} \qquad (7.12)\]
since each subset of the $\binom{n}{2}$ possible edges $v_i v_j$ determines a
graph in $\mathcal{G}_n$.
